notes: Desktop, 390 px and dark screenshots of the landing, report (incl. slider-moved) and connect pages. Highly polished. Source chips have a legend. Outcome bars have a €0 line labelled in words and a dashed worst-case line, the worst case is drawn against spare cash, and 'which guess matters most' is explained in words. The slider's line, readout and 'Why this changed' move together (slider-moved: 11 a day, +€133). The phone and dark views hold up, and the connect page has copy buttons for each app. Held back: the rehearsal, the most original visual, looks dead in the demo: mostly 'Not around', 0 of 6 tried or told anyone (report.txt:533-560). The landing teaser shows 'Mia told Jonas' and '3 of 6 tried it' with other names. The report is long (23,943 px at 390 px), and step 2 shows about 24 numbers before any outcome. '−€56.02' keeps its cents next to whole euros, and 'Why this changed' (+€12.40 × 10 − €180) is −€56.00 by hand. The landing page says seven steps where the report has six, and the hero's expected line ends above break-even while the demo's ends below.
improvements: Report step 5 (src/report/demo.ts, src/report/rehearsal.ts) and the landing rehearsal teaser (site/index.html): make the demo rehearsal show something happening, and make the teaser match it. Today the grid is mostly 'Not around', 'How far it spread' shows 0 of 6 for tried, came back and told someone, and 'Who told whom' has nothing to show. Use a saved AI-played run, or a seed and mix where at least one person tries the deal and one tells a friend, and still label it honestly. Use the same names and counts on the landing teaser (today it shows M, J, A, H, S, L and '3 of 6 tried it'; the demo has Felix to Rafael and 0 tried). Why: this is the original part, and a judge sees an empty grid. Done when report-desktop.png step 5 shows at least one try and one word-of-mouth link, and the landing teaser quotes appear in the demo.

Report step 2 (src/report/sections.ts; report.txt:106-277): cut the wall before the first outcome. Keep 'Guesses nobody knows yet' open. Fold 'Your plan' and 'What your numbers already say' behind one summary line, such as '8 facts from your till · 5 choices you made · 7 sums from them: open'. Why: a judge with five minutes, or an owner on a phone, meets about 24 numbers before seeing a single result, and the phone page is 23,943 px. Done when report-phone.png reaches the big break-even '9' in about half the current scroll.

Report money display (src/report/sections.ts, the slider readout and 'Why this changed'): round test results to whole euros everywhere, or build each displayed sum from the displayed parts. Today '−€56.02' sits next to '−€371' and '+€385', and the 'Why this changed' sum (+€12.40 a day × 10 − €180) gives −€56.00 by hand, not −€56.02 (report.txt:489). Why: this sentence invites the owner to check the maths, so it must check out to the cent or be shown in whole euros. Done when a hand check of every 'Why this changed' sentence matches the shown result.

Landing hero and method section (site/index.html:52-69, 'Seven small steps'): line the landing page up with the demo. The hero illustration shows the expected line ending above break-even, but in the demo report the expected test ends €56 below. Draw the demo's real shape (cautious below, expected just under, optimistic above) and keep the line labels visible without waiting for the animation; in landing-desktop.png the lines are unlabelled. Also either number the report's steps 1-7 with 'After the test' as step 7, or say 'six steps, then learn' on the landing page. Why: the first visual a judge sees should teach the same lesson the demo does. Done when the hero's signs match report step 3 and both pages count the steps the same way.

Report persona cards and checklist (src/report/rehearsal.ts:230 and the attitude badge): remove the 'Your number' chip from 'Check these with real customers', since it is a to-do list, not owner data. Rename the 'Fan' badge where it clashes with 'never been in' (Felix): use 'Likes the idea' or 'Curious'. In report-slider-moved.png, also move the 'Your guess' label off the line. Why: the labels are the AI lesson, so every chip must be right, and small incoherences on the cards cost trust. Done when chips appear only beside values, and no card contradicts itself.
pitchIn60s: Visually it is a teaching report, not a dashboard. Each of the six steps does one job. Every figure wears a source chip, and there is a break-even slider with a plain 'Why this changed' sentence, a worst case shown against spare cash, and a printable test card. It works on a phone and in dark mode. The rehearsal visuals are the weak spot: in the demo they show an empty neighbourhood, and the report runs long before the first result.
standout: The break-even slider: the chart line, the marked break-even, the readout and the 'Why this changed' sentence update together, so the mechanism is visible, not just the new number.
weakest: The demo rehearsal visuals: a grid of 'Not around' squares and 0-of-6 counts. They undersell the most original feature and contradict the landing teaser ('3 of 6 tried it', 'Mia told Jonas').
